core.text: The one stipulated 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and achieved approximately 2.4 percent final-vial spread. It challenges universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and optical stability for this bounded proxy; reliable lower-speed sufficiency remains a hypothesis.

Protect the anomaly: transient bright specks cross the middle region at 900 rpm alongside fluctuating image spread. Their identity and contribution remain unresolved, and matched 900 rpm final-vial readings are absent. Neither bubbles nor actual concentration gradients can be inferred from specks alone.

Proposed discrimination: compare fresh fixed-duration 300 and 900 rpm trials, each stirred for 60 seconds, logging five-second images through cessation and depth samples at second 120. Separately compare timer-stopped and optical-rule-controlled 900 rpm trials, ending by second 105. These four hypothetical trials fit the six-trial limit; use the spill tray and stop if liquid escapes.

residue.text: Retain a third hypothesis: reflections or a persistent optical artifact could produce side-image spread despite passing depth samples. A rapid change after cessation would support an agitation-to-image effect, but would not identify specks or independently establish a disturbance-renewal loop.

Sampling may disturb gradients; alternate depth order and record raw readings. Hold dye-addition location, bottle and camera settings fixed. References establish stipulated repeatability, not concentration calibration, and commanded rpm is unverified.

Report all endpoint failures and stirring durations. Timer and enabled-rule trials may have different quiet intervals, limiting causal attribution. Speed, optical-rule necessity, future success and extension to other liquids remain unresolved.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis A: agitation renews optical disturbance after the depth-sample target is achievable; apparent incompleteness can prolong unnecessary stirring.
tension.account_b: Incompatible hypothesis B: the fluctuating optical spread primarily reflects unresolved dye gradients; continued agitation is needed to achieve the sample target in the proposed comparison.
tension.prediction_a: Fixed-duration cessation would promptly reduce image disturbance, while timer and longer enabled-rule trials would both pass final-vial spread despite shadow-rule failures. This supports A only within the tested comparison.
tension.prediction_b: The timer trial would fail final-vial spread while the longer enabled-rule trial passes; optical spread would not reliably disappear solely upon cessation. Both failing, or persistent images with passing samples, would leave this binary comparison unresolved.
